ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, a right-angled triangle paper has its two right-angled sides measuring $6$ and $8$, respectively. Now, it is folded such that point $A$ coincides with point $B$, with the crease being $DE$. What is the value of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: According to the properties of the fold transformation, we know that $\triangle DBE \cong \triangle DAE$, $\therefore$AD=BD,\\
$\because$ the lengths of the two right-angled sides of the rectangular paper are 6 and 8, respectively, $\therefore$AB=10, $\tan A = \frac{3}{4}$,\\
In $\triangle ADE$, $DE = \tan A \times AD = \boxed{\frac{15}{4}}$.
